title: Hyperbolic links associated to Hamiltonian subgraphs in simple 3-polytopes: links of Hamiltonian theta-subgraphs (printed as Theorem 6.3)
author: Nikolai Erokhovets
work: Hyperbolic links associated to Hamiltonian subgraphs in simple 3-polytopes
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 6.3 (source0.tex lines 1653--1663, source label Th:unl), the three-part classification of the link of a Hamiltonian theta-subgraph in a simple 3-polytope: the circles are mutually unlinked exactly when every matching edge joins vertices of different paths; an unlinked nontrivial link always contains a triple of Borromean rings; and the link is trivial exactly for the pairs obtained from the simplex by cutting off vertices. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1664--1694 (31 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral) and with the example the proof invokes. The proof is a genuine geometric argument rather than a verification: it reads the linking pattern of the circles from the representation of the theta-subgraph on the coordinate rays of the octant, and when a matching edge joins two vertices of one path it produces a contradicting second matching edge by excluding bigonal faces, which links the corresponding circles as a Hopf link; it then shows that if the polytope is not the simplex and the link is unlinked one can always find an edge of the required type and reduce the pair by cutting off a vertex without changing triviality, and that otherwise three successive matching edges of the matching form a triple of Borromean rings, after which the article's Example 6.2 gives the trivial case. The substantive steps are the octant linking computation, the vertex-cutting reduction and the Borromean-ring construction. H2: a complete original research-paper theorem, moderately short, whose proof is a genuinely technical geometric argument.
